newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rebels say one N.Korean ship crew killed.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rebels say one N.Korean ship crew killed.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Tamil Tiger separatists said on Tuesday that one of the 38 crew members of the N.Korean merchant ship they seized earlier was killed in a shootout when he tried to escape.

The clandestine Voice of Tiger radio, monitored in government-held town of Vavuniya, some 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo, said Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels had boarded the ship Morang Bong late on Monday and taken it to their northeastern coastal base of Mulliativu.
A Defence Ministry statement said on Tuesday the North Koran ship was captured by the LTTE while it was some eight km (five miles) off Point Pedro on the former rebel stronghold of Jaffna.

An official of Monsell International, the ship's agent in Colombo, earlier told Reuters that the ship had carried nearly 3,000 tonnes of food and essential items to Point Pedro and was hijacked after it had unloaded its cargo.
The Tiger radio said the rebels were making arrangements to release the remaining crew. It did not give details.

The LTTE are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
